statements.quote: Some American patients with stage 4 lung cancer travel to Cuba to receive CIMAvax , a therapeutic immunotherapy vaccine developed by Cuba's Center of Molecular Immunology.

source.title: CIMAvax: why American lung cancer patients travel to Cuba (Google AI Overview)

statements.availability: The US embargo bans the import of Cuban medicines; patients travel through third countries or carry refrigerated doses back. US clinical trials at Roswell Park, Buffalo, New York.
statements.approval: Developed by Cuba's Center of Molecular Immunology. Not approved by the US FDA.
statements.note: Targets the epidermal growth factor (EGF) that lung cancer cells need; manages the cancer as a chronic condition, without the toxicity of chemotherapy.

statements.quote: CIMAvax was approved in Cuba in 2011. It has since been approved in Argentina, Colombia, Peru, and Paraguay.

source.title: Mad Honey, chapter 4: the pharmaceutical machine (Nir Strulovitz)

statements.availability: Only legal US access: clinical trials at Roswell Park, Buffalo, New York (also combined with nivolumab). Americans have smuggled it in through Canada or Mexico.
statements.approval: Approved in Cuba (2011), Argentina, Colombia, Peru and Paraguay. Not approved by the US FDA.
statements.note: Indicated for advanced non-small cell lung cancer after first-line chemotherapy.
